event: Tsunami from the 22 May 1960 Chile earthquake reaching Hilo, Hawaii

minuteZero.what: Hilo's coastal sirens sound for the first time.
minuteZero.why: The sirens were the public signal to leave the shore, so it is when a coordinator would start calling. The official warning (18:47) went to agencies; the County Civil Defense log records the first siren at 20:35 (USGS Circular 1187 rounds it to 'around 8:30 p.m.').

events.what: Mw 9.5 earthquake off south-central Chile (19:11:20 UTC). Hawaii was on UTC-10:00 in 1960.
US Coast and Geodetic Survey (Honolulu Observatory) issues the tsunami warning; waves expected at Hilo about midnight.
State Civil Defense gives authority to sound the sirens (they had been held at 20:00).
First siren. The Civil Defense log lists soundings at 20:35, 20:40, 20:43, 20:47 and 20:50.
Police told to evacuate low areas immediately.
First rise at the Wailuku River bridge (Cox & Mink: detected in Hilo Bay at 0007 HST). NCEI lists 09:58 UTC (23:58 HST), which conflicts.
events.where: p. 139, via Johnston 2003 pp. 8-9, 33-36; Cox & Mink 1963 abstract

events.what: Wave 1 crest, about 4 ft above normal water at the bridge.
Wave 2 crest, about 9 ft above normal; floods Kamehameha Ave and the business district. Agency logs: water over the pier 00:47, Kamehameha Ave covered from Hilo Theater to Waiakea about 00:55-00:58.
Trough about 7 ft below normal; the bore's rumble is heard.
Wave 3 arrives as a bore about 20 ft high at the bridge; the Waiakea town clock stops at 01:04. Runup reaches 35 ft (10.7 m).
Bore reaches the power plant and the city goes dark.
Eaton's record shows smaller crests (about 6-8.5 ft at the bridge) continuing to about 2 a.m.; Volcano Watch counts eight waves cresting 4-14 ft at the bridge. Figure values, not a table.
events.where: p. 7 figure; USGS Volcano Watch 20 May 1994

outcome.injured: 282 (Cox & Mink 1963; USGS Circular 1187); 43 seriously injured (Lander & Lockridge 1989)
